findings.title: Legacy TaskExecutor can ignore stop signal while runtime acknowledges and requeues
findings.requirement: A normal re-dispatch waits for actual Worker stop acknowledgement; stale execution must not be treated as safely stopped.
findings.evidence: The default stop-aware overload delegates to the legacy one-argument method without observing the BooleanSupplier. WorkerRuntime acknowledges whenever that method returns after a stop signal, then control-plane acknowledgement requeues the task.
findings.required_change: Require explicit stop-aware execution or a confirmed cancellation result; never convert a normal return from a non-cooperative executor into stop acknowledgement. Add a behavior scenario for legacy/lambda executors.

findings.title: Duplicate stop acknowledgement is rejected instead of being idempotent
findings.requirement: FD Work Item 1.3 and Tester scenario S07 require idempotent stop acknowledgement.
findings.evidence: The first acknowledgement changes the attempt to EXPIRED and requeues the task. A duplicate is rejected because the task is no longer RUNNING; the repository update also only accepts an attempt in RUNNING state.
findings.required_change: Return success for a repeated acknowledgement of the same task, worker, and lease without requeueing or releasing resources twice; continue rejecting mismatched identities. Add duplicate/retry behavior coverage.
